job: Job 6 - Website form -> Zendesk -> AI email agent -> free VA
summary: Client photos in a Zendesk ticket, booking done by our AI agent 'Bruce', video call, estimate

people.who: Bruce - our AI email agent, inside Zendesk

client_concern: Website form: 'Mold on ceiling in bathroom shower and around edge of bathtub where caulking is. There is a bathroom fan that is used regularly.' The client uploaded 2 photos with the form. She had an older quote from us and in May 2026 texted that she wanted to go ahead with it.

timeline.what: Client fills in the form on her iPhone and uploads 2 photos. A Zendesk ticket is created by email.
Bruce thanks her for the photos and suggests the free virtual inspection as the first step.
Client: 'Let's go ahead and book'. Bruce offers 2 slots for the next day; client picks 9:00 AM.
Bruce confirms. Calendar event created: 'Booked by Bruce Text AI Agent', with the Zendesk link. 37 minutes from form to booking, no human involved.
8-minute call. From about 0:40 to 6:30 the client walks the camera through the bathroom (shower ceiling, tub, toilet area).
SMS asking the client to rate the VA app.
Inspector posts the booking details and 7 photos ('Area of concern').
Estimate MO971 ($1,495 + HST) sent. No report - free VAs get an estimate only.
4 follow-up SMS, the last one: 'still interested... or should we close your case?'
Support follows up by hand (screenshot posted in Asana) and closes the card.
Lead moved to 'Monthly follow up'. An SMS signed by the inspector and an email 'A Special Gift to Thank You for Your Trust!'.

findings: Bathroom: mold on the ceiling corner above the shower and along the tub caulking (from the photos and the video call).
recommendations: Remove the silicone sealant; treat tiles, grout and the drywall ceiling
Keep humidity at 30-50%; make sure the fan is adequate and clean; consider a dehumidifier

estimate_summary.status: Viewed, not accepted. Lead moved to 'Monthly follow up'.
scope: Containment of the bathroom, negative pressure if possible
Remove silicone sealant; treat tiles, grout, drywall ceiling
HEPA vacuum + fogging; swab test; Project Clearance Report

estimate_items_from_freshbooks.description:
The inspector who prepared this estimate is:
Luka Markovic, MSC ME, CMI

Got questions? Contact Luka by phone at: 343-600-3453, or by email: luka@bustmold.com

--1 - Containment of Contaminated Area(s)
Containment of the bathroom with polyethylene drop sheets and zipper door(s), using negative air pressure (if permitted by actual conditions at the property), or an equivalent method, in order to prevent the cross-contamination of mold spores, dust/debris, and other particulates to other areas of the property.

Additionally, any personal belongings or large items that cannot be relocated within the affected area will be individually wrapped to protect them against dust and debris during the remediation process.

--2 - Removal of Affected Components
Removal & disposal of compromised, contaminated and/or moldy materials from the bathroom, as assessed during the initial inspection, in accordance with mold removal guidelines - https://iaq.is/mold-removal-guidelines

 - Location: Bathroom -

Materials which will be removed and disposed of include:
• silicone sealant
• any other organic-based materials on an as-needed basis.

Any affected structural or framing components will be topically, manually and/or abrasively treated prior to the disinfection process.

-Topical Treatment Process:
Removal of mold from the areas by means of manual wirebrushing, or other topical and abrasive removal techniques. This is done in conjunction with HEPA vacuuming, and the application of an advanced, two-stage mold remediation protocol, initiating with high-precision stain removal techniques to revitalize the aesthetics of affected surfaces. This is seamlessly followed by the strategic application of our proprietary fungicides, meticulously designed to eliminate mold spores, thereby ensuring your space is restored to its pristine condition and safeguarded against future contamination.

The areas & materials that require treatment are:
Bathroom:
- tiles
- grout
- drywall ceiling
- other general surface areas as required

Residual non-fungal staining may be present upon completion.

All removed materials will be properly packaged in 6ml double bags and will be appropriately disposed of in a discreet fashion.

Mold Busters' trained remediation professionals are recommended to wear dust impermeable gloves, half-face air purifying respirator (P-100), full body dust-impervious coveralls, and boot covers or separate work boots.

Price includes labor, material, travel, disposal, and equipment fees.
Any additional items and areas that require removal or treatment are subject to revision and discussion with the client.

- In the case additional layers of drywall and flooring are found during the remediation project, a scope increase will be presented to the client for consideration

-- 3 - Cleaning and Disinfection
Thorough HEPA vacuuming is conducted throughout all surfaces in the affected bathroom area in order to remove mold spores, particulates, and dust.

All remaining surfaces (studs, beams, walls, floors, etc.) in the bathroom will be disinfected, by concentrated fogging, using an approved fungicide. 

Additional vacuuming or HEPA air scrubbing may occur upon completion of the fogging process, along with a general cleaning of all areas traveled by Mold Busters personnel.

Mold Busters applies an advanced, two-stage mold remediation protocol, initiating with high-precision stain removal techniques to revitalize the aesthetics of affected surfaces. This is seamlessly followed by the strategic application of our proprietary fungicides, meticulously designed to eliminate mold spores, thereby ensuring your space is restored to its pristine condition and safeguarded against future contamination.

-- 4 - Post-Removal Clearance (Swab)
Post-remediation verification is conducted to ensure that the environment has been successfully remediated.

The final clearance inspection includes a visual inspection and an instant swab analysis.

This will be performed by the Project Supervisor upon completion of the remediation process.

-- Project Clearance Report
A written report following the remediation process, describing the outcome of the remediation work, any potential source issues, clearance grades, etc.

Additional recommendations will be made in this report to assist in preventing future fungal contamination.

-- Notes
"

Estimated Project Time: 4 hours

Please note that this is only an estimated timeframe provided for your reference. We do not charge by the hour—our pricing is all-inclusive, covering time, travel, labour, materials, and disposal for the full scope of work.",
